hints.title: Subarray Sum Monotonicity
hints.text: To maximize partitioned array length, each merged block should have the smallest possible sum that is at least as large as the previous block sum.

hints.title: Dynamic Programming State
hints.text: Let dp[i] be the maximum non-decreasing length for prefix i, and last[i] be the sum of the last block in that optimal partition.

hints.title: Monotonic Queue Transition
hints.text: The valid transition condition is pref[i] >= pref[j] + last[j]. Maintain candidate indices j in a deque ordered by pref[j] + last[j].

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def findMaximumLength(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        pref = [0] * (n + 1)
        for i in range(n):
            pref[i + 1] = pref[i] + nums[i]
            
        dp = [0] * (n + 1)
        last = [0] * (n + 1)
        dq = deque([0])
        
        for i in range(1, n + 1):
            while len(dq) > 1 and pref[dq[1]] + last[dq[1]] <= pref[i]:
                dq.popleft()
            j = dq[0]
            dp[i] = dp[j] + 1
            last[i] = pref[i] - pref[j]
            while dq and pref[dq[-1]] + last[dq[-1]] >= pref[i] + last[i]:
                dq.pop()
            dq.append(i)
        return dp[n]
```

complexity.notes: Amortized linear time with monotonic queue state optimization.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: O(n^2) DP times out for n = 10^5.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(n) auxiliary memory for DP table, last values, and deque.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognize that prefix sums plus previous block sums form a monotonic threshold.
